tagline: The spec sheet is a marketing document. We check it against the standard.

author.name: The PanelProof Editorial Desk
author.bio: PanelProof does not operate a measurement lab, and says so. What it does is read the documents almost nobody reads end to end - the VESA DisplayHDR and ClearMR compliance test specifications, panel-maker datasheets, HDMI and DisplayPort feature tables, and the published measurement data from independent labs - and reconcile them against what manufacturers print on the box. Every claim is traced to the standard or the measurement it came from, with the revision and the date it was current.

footer_blurb: Independent analysis of display specifications, certification standards and panel technology. We reconcile marketing claims against published standards and independent lab measurements, and we cite both.
disclaimer_line: Nothing here substitutes for measuring your own unit, and panel behaviour varies between production runs

homepage.title: PanelProof - display specs, checked against the standard

homepage.h1: The number on the box, and the number that matters
homepage.dek: Most display specifications are unregulated, self-reported and measured however the manufacturer prefers. PanelProof reads the certification standards and the independent lab data, and tells you which claims are load-bearing.

llms_blurb: Independent analysis of display specifications, certification standards and panel technology for monitors, TVs and laptop screens.
sourcing_note: Claims are traced to primary sources - VESA compliance test specifications, panel-maker datasheets, HDMI Forum and VESA standards documentation, manufacturer specification pages and published independent lab measurements - with the specification revision and the date the figure was current. PanelProof does not operate its own measurement lab and does not present third-party measurements as its own. Content is drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by a human editor; see /editorial-policy/.

factcheck.note: Every post carries per-figure source indices; validate.py fails the build otherwise. A primary source here means a standards-body compliance document (VESA, HDMI Forum, ITU-R), a panel-maker datasheet, a manufacturer specification page, or a named independent lab's published measurement.
